newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds suffer after strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds suffer after strong U.S. data.

text.p: German Bunds extended losses, flirting with session lows, late Friday, falling victim to sharply higher U.S. economic data which has firmed up fears that interest rates may soon turn higher.

Bunds closed Frankfurt trading down 20 basis points at 97.18 having traded between 97.14 and 97.39. Dealers said they were now not terribly optimistic that the market will move higher early next week.
"We were looking at closing above 97.30 a few days ago and now that is a goal that is not in immediate sight anymore," a dealer said.
News that the Chicago Purchasing Managers index rose to 60.0 in August from 51.2 in July took markets by surprise, sending Treasuries sharply lower.
In turn Bunds also fell, even though they still outperformed the U.S. Treasury market.
Traders said fears were beginning to mass that the U.S. Fed would not be able to wait much longer to raise interest rates, even after rates were left unchanged last week.
Even the Bundesbank's 30 basis point cut in the securities repurchase agreement last week, failed to inspire the market, a dealer said, adding "Technically the market isn't strong now."
